label: thm:mainA
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:mainA}
Let $(M^n,g)$ be a connected Riemannian manifold with harmonic curvature, and suppose that $\operatorname{Ric}_k\geq0$ for some $1\leq k\leq n-2$. Then the Ricci tensor has constant rank on $M$. Moreover, its nullity distribution $\mathcal N=\ker\operatorname{Ric}$ is a parallel subbundle of $TM$.

If, in addition, $(M^n,g)$ is complete, then its universal cover splits isometrically as
\[
(\widetilde M,\widetilde g)
=
\mathbb R^m\times(N^{n-m},g_N),
\]
where $m=\dim\ker\operatorname{Ric}$ and the Ricci tensor of $N$ is positive definite.
head: environment

label: thm:counterexample
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:counterexample}
For every $n\geq4$, there exists a connected Riemannian manifold $(M^n,g)$ with harmonic curvature and $\operatorname{Ric}\geq0$ such that the Ricci tensor does not have constant rank.
head: environment

label: cor:four-dimensional-classification
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:four-dimensional-classification}
Let $(M^4,g)$ be a complete Riemannian four-manifold with harmonic
curvature and $\operatorname{Ric}_2\geq0$. If the Ricci tensor is not positive
definite, then its universal cover is isometric to one of
\[
\mathbb R^4,\qquad
\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb S^2(c),\qquad
\mathbb R\times\mathbb S^3(c),
\]
where $c>0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:mainA}, the Ricci tensor has constant rank and
\[
\widetilde M=\mathbb R^{4-r}\times N^r,
\qquad
\operatorname{Ric}_N>0,
\]
where $r=\operatorname{rank}\operatorname{Ric}$.

If $r=0$, then $\operatorname{Ric}\equiv0$, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:null-jacobi} implies that the metric is flat.
Thus $\widetilde M\cong\mathbb R^4$.

The case $r=1$ is impossible, since every one-dimensional manifold has
identically vanishing Ricci curvature.

If $r=2$, then $N^2$ has positive constant Gaussian curvature. Since
$N^2$ is complete and simply connected, it is isometric to a round
sphere $\mathbb S^2(c)$ for some $c>0$.

Finally, suppose $r=3$. Then
\[
\widetilde M=\mathbb R\times N^3.
\]
The factor $N^3$ is complete and simply connected, has positive Ricci
curvature and constant scalar curvature, and its Ricci tensor is
Codazzi. In dimension three this implies that the Cotton tensor
vanishes, so $N^3$ is locally conformally flat. By the classification
theorem of Hu--Li--Simon \cite{HuLiSimon}, a complete locally
conformally flat three-manifold with constant scalar curvature and
nonnegative Ricci curvature has universal cover isometric to one of
\[
\mathbb S^3(c),\qquad
\mathbb R^3,\qquad
\mathbb R\times\mathbb S^2(c).
\]
Since $N^3$ is already simply connected and $\operatorname{Ric}_N>0$, the latter two
possibilities are excluded. Hence
\[
N^3\cong\mathbb S^3(c).
\]
head: environment

label: thm:mainB
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:mainB}
Let $(M^n,g,f)$ be a connected gradient Ricci soliton satisfying
\[
\operatorname{Ric}+\nabla^2 f=\lambda g
\]
for some constant $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. Suppose that
$
\operatorname{Ric}_k\geq0
$
for some $1\leq k\leq n-2$. Then the Ricci tensor has constant rank on $M$. Moreover, its nullity distribution
$
\mathcal N=\ker\operatorname{Ric}
$
is a parallel subbundle of $TM$.

If, in addition, $(M^n,g)$ is complete and
$
m=\dim\ker\operatorname{Ric},
$
then its universal cover splits isometrically as
\[
(\widetilde M,\widetilde g)
=
\mathbb R^m\times(N^{n-m},g_N),
\]
where $\operatorname{Ric}_{g_N}>0$. Furthermore, the lift of the soliton potential splits as
\begin{equation}\label{eq:potential-splitting}
\widetilde f(x,y)
=
\frac{\lambda}{2}|x|^2+\langle a,x\rangle+f_N(y)+C.
\end{equation}
for some $a\in\mathbb R^m$ and $C\in\mathbb R$, where
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_{g_N}+\nabla_N^2f_N=\lambda g_N.
\]
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Related rigidity and compactness results for shrinking gradient Ricci
solitons under curvature conditions weaker than nonnegative sectional
curvature were obtained by Wu--Wu \cite{Wu-Wu}. In particular,
nonnegative second-intermediate Ricci curvature implies the curvature
pinching condition considered there. We emphasize that
Theorem~\ref{thm:mainB} is a local constant-rank statement and applies to shrinking,
steady, and expanding gradient Ricci solitons.
head: environment

label: thm:soliton-sharpness
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:soliton-sharpness}
For every $n\geq4$, there exists a connected gradient shrinking Ricci
soliton $(M^n,g,f)$ with nonnegative Ricci curvature,
such that the Ricci tensor does not have constant rank.
head: environment

label: lem:intermediate-algebra
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:k-smallest
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a unit vector $X$, and let $e_1,\ldots,e_{n-1}$ be an orthonormal basis of $X^\perp$. Set $\kappa_\alpha=K(X,e_\alpha)$ and, after relabeling, assume
$
\kappa_1\leq\kappa_2\leq\cdots\leq\kappa_{n-1}.
$
The condition $\operatorname{Ric}_k\geq0$ implies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:k-smallest}
\kappa_1+\cdots+\kappa_k\geq0.
\end{equation}
In particular, $\kappa_k\geq0$, and hence $\kappa_\alpha\geq0$ for all $\alpha\geq k$. It follows immediately that
\[
\operatorname{Ric}(X,X)=\sum_{\alpha=1}^{n-1}\kappa_\alpha\geq0.
\]
Since $X$ was arbitrary, $\operatorname{Ric}\geq0$.

For $k=1$, \eqref{eq:sectional-lower-bound} is precisely the assumption of nonnegative sectional curvature. We therefore assume $k\geq2$. There is nothing to prove if $\kappa_1\geq0$. Suppose that $\kappa_1=-a<0$. By~\eqref{eq:k-smallest},
\[
\kappa_2+\cdots+\kappa_k\geq a.
\]
Since $\kappa_2\leq\cdots\leq\kappa_k$, we obtain
$
\kappa_k\geq\frac{a}{k-1}.
$
Consequently, $\kappa_\alpha\geq a/(k-1)$ for every $\alpha\geq k+1$. Using again~\eqref{eq:k-smallest}, we find
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Ric}(X,X)
&=\sum_{\alpha=1}^{k}\kappa_\alpha
+\sum_{\alpha=k+1}^{n-1}\kappa_\alpha\\
&\geq\frac{n-1-k}{k-1}a.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus
\[
a\leq\frac{k-1}{n-1-k}\operatorname{Ric}(X,X),
\]
which proves~\eqref{eq:sectional-lower-bound}.
head: environment

label: cor:null-jacobi
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By~\eqref{eq:sectional-lower-bound}, $K(V,X)\geq0$ for every unit vector $X\perp V$, since $\operatorname{Ric}(V,V)=0$. On the other hand,
\[
0=\operatorname{Ric}(V,V)=\sum_{\alpha=1}^{n-1}K(V,e_\alpha)
\]
for any orthonormal basis of $V^\perp$. Hence every summand vanishes, proving~\eqref{eq:null-sectional}. Polarizing the quadratic form $X\mapsto R(V,X,V,X)$ gives~\eqref{eq:null-jacobi-tensor}.
head: environment

label: lem:subtrace-viscosity
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:subtrace-viscosity}
Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor on $M$, and fix $p\in M$.
Choose an orthonormal eigenbasis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $A$ at $p$, with
eigenvalues $\lambda_1\leq\cdots\leq\lambda_n$. If $\xi$ is a $C^2$
lower support function for $\sigma_\ell(A)$ at $p$, then for every
$X\in T_pM$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:subtrace-gradient}
\nabla_X\xi(p)
=
\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}(\nabla_XA)(e_i,e_i),
\end{equation}
and
\[
\Delta\xi(p)\leq\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}(\Delta A)(e_i,e_i).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Extend $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ to local orthonormal vector fields
$E_1,\ldots,E_n$ by radial parallel transport from $p$. Then
\[
\xi(q)\leq \sigma_\ell(A)(q)
\leq \sum_{i=1}^{\ell}A(E_i,E_i)(q)
\]
near $p$, and equality holds at $p$. Hence the first derivatives agree
at $p$, which gives \eqref{eq:subtrace-gradient}. Taking second
derivatives along geodesics issuing from $p$ and summing over an
orthonormal basis yields
\[
\Delta\xi(p)\leq
\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}(\Delta A)(e_i,e_i).
\]
head: environment

label: prop:subtrace-inequality
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\xi$ be any smooth lower support for $\sigma_\ell$ at $p$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:subtrace-viscosity} and~\eqref{eq:ric-component-estimate},
\[
\Delta\xi(p)
\leq
\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}(\Delta\operatorname{Ric})_{ii}
\leq
\frac{n-2}{n-1-k}R
\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\lambda_i
=
\frac{n-2}{n-1-k}R\,\sigma_\ell(p).
\]
This is precisely~\eqref{eq:main-subtrace} in the viscosity sense.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $R=0$, then $\operatorname{Ric}\geq0$ immediately implies $\operatorname{Ric}\equiv0$, and there is nothing to prove. We may therefore assume $R>0$.

Let
\[
m=\max_{x\in M}\dim\ker\operatorname{Ric}_x.
\]
If $m=0$, then $\operatorname{Ric}>0$ everywhere and the assertion follows. Suppose $m\geq1$, and choose $p\in M$ with $\dim\ker\operatorname{Ric}_p=m$. Then $\sigma_m(p)=0$, while $\sigma_m\geq0$ on $M$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:subtrace-inequality},
\[
\Delta\sigma_m
-
\frac{n-2}{n-1-k}R\,\sigma_m
\leq0
\]
in the viscosity sense. The strong minimum principle implies $\sigma_m\equiv0$ on the connected manifold $M$.

Thus $\dim\ker\operatorname{Ric}_x\geq m$ for every $x\in M$. By the definition of $m$, equality must hold everywhere. Hence $\operatorname{Ric}$ has constant rank.
head: environment

label: prop:nullity-parallel
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:nullity-parallel}
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:mainA}, the distribution $\mathcal N=\ker\operatorname{Ric}$ is parallel.
head: environment

label: eq:nullity-bochner-1
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $V$ be a local smooth section of $\mathcal N$. Thus $\operatorname{Ric}(V,\cdot)=0$, and in particular $\operatorname{Ric}(V,V)\equiv0$. Let $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ be a local orthonormal frame which is normal at a fixed point. Differentiating twice gives
\begin{align}
0
&=
\Delta\bigl(\operatorname{Ric}(V,V)\bigr)\nonumber\\
&=
(\Delta\operatorname{Ric})(V,V)
+
4\sum_a(\nabla_{e_a}\operatorname{Ric})(\nabla_{e_a}V,V)
+
2\operatorname{Ric}(\Delta V,V)\nonumber\\
&\qquad
+
2\sum_a\operatorname{Ric}(\nabla_{e_a}V,\nabla_{e_a}V).
\label{eq:nullity-bochner-1}
\end{align}
Since $V\in\ker\operatorname{Ric}$, we have $\operatorname{Ric}(\Delta V,V)=0$ and $\operatorname{Ric}(\nabla_{e_a}V,V)=0$. Differentiating the latter identity and summing over $a$ yields
\[
\sum_a(\nabla_{e_a}\operatorname{Ric})(\nabla_{e_a}V,V)
=
-\sum_a\operatorname{Ric}(\nabla_{e_a}V,\nabla_{e_a}V).
\]
Substituting into~\eqref{eq:nullity-bochner-1}, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nullity-bochner-2}
0
=
(\Delta\operatorname{Ric})(V,V)
-
2\sum_a\operatorname{Ric}(\nabla_{e_a}V,\nabla_{e_a}V).
\end{equation}

By~\eqref{eq:ricci-laplacian},
\[
(\Delta\operatorname{Ric})(V,V)
=
|\operatorname{Ric}(V,\cdot)|^2
-
R(V,e_i,V,e_j)R_{ij}.
\]
The first term vanishes because $V\in\ker\operatorname{Ric}$, while the second vanishes by Corollary~\ref{cor:null-jacobi}. Hence $(\Delta\operatorname{Ric})(V,V)=0$. Equation~\eqref{eq:nullity-bochner-2} therefore gives
\[
\sum_a\operatorname{Ric}(\nabla_{e_a}V,\nabla_{e_a}V)=0.
\]
Since $\operatorname{Ric}\geq0$, every term on the left-hand side is nonnegative. Consequently, $\operatorname{Ric}(\nabla_XV,\nabla_XV)=0$ for every tangent vector $X$, and hence $\nabla_XV\in\ker\operatorname{Ric}$. Thus $\mathcal N$ is parallel.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume now that $(M,g)$ is complete. The lift of $\mathcal N$ to the universal cover $(\widetilde M,\widetilde g)$ is a parallel distribution, and so is its orthogonal complement. By the de Rham decomposition theorem,
\[
(\widetilde M,\widetilde g)
=
(M_0^m,g_0)\times(N^{n-m},g_N),
\]
where $m=\dim\ker\operatorname{Ric}$.

For every $V\in TM_0$, Corollary~\ref{cor:null-jacobi} gives $R(V,\cdot,V,\cdot)=0$. In particular, all sectional curvatures of $M_0$ vanish. Since $M_0$ is complete and simply connected, $(M_0,g_0)\cong\mathbb R^m$. Finally, the kernel of the Ricci tensor is exactly the tangent bundle of the Euclidean factor, and hence $\operatorname{Ric}_{g_N}>0$. Therefore
\[
(\widetilde M,\widetilde g)
\cong
\mathbb R^m\times(N^{n-m},g_N),
\qquad
\operatorname{Ric}_{g_N}>0.
\]
head: environment

label: lem:codazzi-warp
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The connection formulas for the multiply warped product give
\[
\nabla_{e_A}e_0=ae_A,
\qquad
\nabla_{e_3}e_0=be_3.
\]
Since the Ricci tensor is diagonal and its eigenvalues depend only on $t$,
\[
(\nabla_{e_0}\operatorname{Ric})(e_A,e_A)=\rho_1',
\qquad
(\nabla_{e_A}\operatorname{Ric})(e_0,e_A)=a(\rho_0-\rho_1).
\]
Thus the Codazzi equation in the $e_0,e_A$ directions is precisely~\eqref{eq:codazzi-rho1}. Similarly,
\[
(\nabla_{e_0}\operatorname{Ric})(e_3,e_3)=\rho_3',
\qquad
(\nabla_{e_3}\operatorname{Ric})(e_0,e_3)=b(\rho_0-\rho_3),
\]
which gives~\eqref{eq:codazzi-rho3}. All remaining Codazzi equations are automatic by the symmetry of the warped product. Finally, by the second Bianchi identity, the Ricci tensor is Codazzi if and only if the Riemann curvature tensor is divergence-free.
head: environment

label: prop:4d-counterexample
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:4d-counterexample}
There exists $\varepsilon>0$ and a smooth metric
\[
g=dt^2+f(t)^2g_{\mathbb S^2}+h(t)^2d\theta^2
\]
on $(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times\mathbb S^2\times\mathbb S^1$ such that $\delta\operatorname{Rm}=0$, $\operatorname{Ric}\geq0$, and
\[
\operatorname{rank}\operatorname{Ric}
=
\begin{cases}
2,&t=0,\\
4,&0<|t|<\varepsilon.
\end{cases}
\]
In particular, the Ricci tensor does not have constant rank.
head: environment

label: rem:ric2-fails
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:ric2-fails}
The example also shows explicitly how ordinary nonnegative Ricci curvature permits a cancellation which is ruled out by intermediate Ricci curvature. At $t=0$, formulas~\eqref{eq:K0A}--\eqref{eq:KA3} give
\[
K_{01}=K_{02}=-1,
\qquad
K_{12}=1,
\qquad
K_{03}=3,
\qquad
K_{13}=K_{23}=0.
\]
Hence
\[
\operatorname{Ric}(e_1,e_1)
=
K_{10}+K_{12}+K_{13}
=
-1+1+0
=
0,
\]
while $K_{10}+K_{13}=-1<0$. Thus $\operatorname{Ric}\geq0$ but $\operatorname{Ric}_2\not\geq0$. This is precisely the cancellation mechanism excluded by Lemma~\ref{lem:intermediate-algebra}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $n=4$, the conclusion is Proposition~\ref{prop:4d-counterexample}.

Let $n>4$, and let $(M^4,g)$ be the four-dimensional example above. Consider
\[
(\widehat M^n,\widehat g)
=
(M^4,g)\times(\mathbb R^{n-4},g_{\mathrm{Euc}}).
\]
The Ricci tensor of the product is $\operatorname{Ric}_{\widehat g}=\operatorname{Ric}_g\oplus0$. Since $\operatorname{Ric}_g$ is Codazzi and the Euclidean factor is flat, $\operatorname{Ric}_{\widehat g}$ is again Codazzi. Hence $\delta\operatorname{Rm}_{\widehat g}=0$, and furthermore $\operatorname{Ric}_{\widehat g}\geq0$.

At points with $t=0$, $\operatorname{rank}\operatorname{Ric}_{\widehat g}=2$, whereas for $0<|t|<\varepsilon$, $\operatorname{rank}\operatorname{Ric}_{\widehat g}=4$. Thus the Ricci tensor does not have constant rank. This proves the theorem in every dimension $n\geq4$.
head: environment

label: prop:soliton-subtrace
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $p\in M$, and let $\xi$ be a smooth lower support for
$\sigma_\ell$ at $p$. Choose an orthonormal Ricci eigenbasis
$e_1,\ldots,e_n$ at $p$ corresponding to the eigenvalues
$\mu_1\leq\cdots\leq\mu_n$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:subtrace-viscosity},
\[
\Delta\xi(p)
\leq
\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}(\Delta\operatorname{Ric})(e_i,e_i),
\]
while \eqref{eq:subtrace-gradient} gives
\[
\nabla_X\xi(p)
=
\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}
(\nabla_X\operatorname{Ric})(e_i,e_i)
\]
for every $X\in T_pM$. Taking $X=\nabla f$, we therefore obtain
\[
\Delta_f\xi(p)
\leq
\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}
(\Delta_f\operatorname{Ric})(e_i,e_i).
\]
Applying \eqref{eq:weighted-component-estimate} yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta_f\xi(p)
&\leq
\bigl(2\lambda+2c_{n,k}R(p)\bigr)
\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\mu_i\\
&=
\bigl(2\lambda+2c_{n,k}R(p)\bigr)
\sigma_\ell(p),
\end{aligned}
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:soliton-subtrace}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let
$
m=\max_{x\in M}\dim\ker\operatorname{Ric}_x.
$
If $m=0$, then $\operatorname{Ric}>0$ everywhere and there is nothing to prove.
Suppose $m\geq1$ and choose $p\in M$ such that
$\dim\ker\operatorname{Ric}_p=m$. Then
$
\sigma_m(p)=0,
$ and $
\sigma_m\geq0.
$

Let $\Omega$ be a connected relatively compact neighborhood
of $p$. Since the scalar curvature is smooth, there exists a constant
$C_\Omega\geq0$ such that
\[
2\lambda+2c_{n,k}R\leq C_\Omega
\]
on $\Omega$. Proposition~\ref{prop:soliton-subtrace} gives
\[
\Delta_f\sigma_m-C_\Omega\sigma_m\leq0
\]
in the viscosity sense on $\Omega$. Since $\sigma_m\geq0$ and
$\sigma_m(p)=0$, the strong maximum principle implies
$\sigma_m\equiv0$ on $\Omega$.

It follows that the zero set of $\sigma_m$ is both open and closed.
Since $M$ is connected and nonempty, we conclude that
\[
\sigma_m\equiv0
\]
on $M$. Hence $\dim\ker\operatorname{Ric}_x\geq m$ for every $x\in M$. By the
definition of $m$, equality holds everywhere, and therefore the Ricci
tensor has constant rank.
head: environment

label: prop:soliton-nullity-parallel
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: eq:soliton-nullity-bochner
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $V$ be a local smooth section of $\mathcal N$. Then
$\operatorname{Ric}(V,\cdot)=0$, and in particular
$
\operatorname{Ric}(V,V)\equiv0.
$ Applying $\Delta_f$ to this identity gives, at a point where
$\{e_a\}$ is a normal orthonormal frame,
\begin{align}
0
&=
\Delta_f\bigl(\operatorname{Ric}(V,V)\bigr)\nonumber\\
&=
(\Delta_f\operatorname{Ric})(V,V)
+
4\sum_a
(\nabla_{e_a}\operatorname{Ric})(\nabla_{e_a}V,V)\nonumber\\
&\qquad
+
2\operatorname{Ric}(\Delta_fV,V)
+
2\sum_a
\operatorname{Ric}(\nabla_{e_a}V,\nabla_{e_a}V).
\label{eq:soliton-nullity-bochner}
\end{align}
Since $V\in\ker\operatorname{Ric}$, we have
$\operatorname{Ric}(\Delta_fV,V)=0$. Moreover,
$\operatorname{Ric}(\nabla_{e_a}V,V)=0$. Differentiating the latter identity and
summing over $a$ yields
\[
\sum_a
(\nabla_{e_a}\operatorname{Ric})(\nabla_{e_a}V,V)
=
-
\sum_a
\operatorname{Ric}(\nabla_{e_a}V,\nabla_{e_a}V).
\]
Thus \eqref{eq:soliton-nullity-bochner} becomes
\begin{equation}\label{eq:soliton-nullity-bochner2}
0
=
(\Delta_f\operatorname{Ric})(V,V)
-
2\sum_a
\operatorname{Ric}(\nabla_{e_a}V,\nabla_{e_a}V).
\end{equation}

On the other hand, by \eqref{eq:weighted-ricci},
\[
(\Delta_f\operatorname{Ric})(V,V)
=
2\lambda\operatorname{Ric}(V,V)
-
2R(V,e_i,V,e_j)R_{ij}.
\]
Both terms on the right-hand side vanish: the first because
$V\in\ker\operatorname{Ric}$, and the second by
\eqref{eq:soliton-null-jacobi}. Therefore
\[
(\Delta_f\operatorname{Ric})(V,V)=0.
\]
It follows from \eqref{eq:soliton-nullity-bochner2} that
\[
\sum_a
\operatorname{Ric}(\nabla_{e_a}V,\nabla_{e_a}V)=0.
\]
Since $\operatorname{Ric}\geq0$, every summand is nonnegative. Hence
\[
\operatorname{Ric}(\nabla_XV,\nabla_XV)=0
\]
for every vector field $X$, and therefore
$\nabla_XV\in\ker\operatorname{Ric}$. Thus $\mathcal N$ is parallel.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume that $(M,g)$ is complete. Since $\mathcal N$ is parallel, its
lift to the universal cover is parallel, as is its orthogonal
complement. By the de Rham decomposition theorem,
\[
(\widetilde M,\widetilde g)
=
(M_0^m,g_0)\times(N^{n-m},g_N),
\]
where $m=\dim\ker\operatorname{Ric}$.

For $V\in TM_0$, \eqref{eq:soliton-null-jacobi} implies that every
sectional curvature containing $V$ vanishes. In particular, $M_0$ is
flat. Since it is complete and simply connected,
$
(M_0,g_0)\cong\mathbb R^m.
$
Moreover, the kernel of the Ricci tensor is precisely the tangent bundle
of the Euclidean factor, and hence
$
\operatorname{Ric}_{g_N}>0.
$

It remains to describe the potential. Let $\widetilde f$ be the lift of
$f$ to $\widetilde M=\mathbb R^m\times N$. The mixed components of the
soliton equation give
\[
\nabla^2\widetilde f(X,Y)=0, \quad  X\in T\mathbb R^m,\quad Y\in TN.
\]
Hence
\[
\widetilde f(x,y)=f_0(x)+f_N(y)+C.
\]
Restricting \eqref{eq:soliton-equation} to the Euclidean factor gives
$
\nabla_{\mathbb R^m}^2f_0=\lambda g_{\mathrm{Euc}},
$
and therefore
$
f_0(x)=\frac{\lambda}{2}|x|^2+\langle a,x\rangle.
$
Restricting the soliton equation to $N$ gives
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_{g_N}+\nabla_N^2f_N=\lambda g_N.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:potential-splitting} and completes the proof.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
When $\lambda\neq0$, a translation in the Euclidean factor removes the
linear term $\langle a,x\rangle$ in
\eqref{eq:potential-splitting}. Thus, up to translation, the Euclidean
factor carries the standard Gaussian shrinking or expanding soliton
potential $\lambda|x|^2/2$. In the steady case $\lambda=0$, the
Euclidean component of the potential is affine.
head: environment

label: prop:shrinker-4d-counterexample
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:shrinker-4d-counterexample}
There exists a four-dimensional gradient shrinking Ricci soliton
$(M_\varepsilon,g,\phi)$ satisfying
\[
\operatorname{Ric}+\nabla^2\phi=\frac{1}{2}g,
\qquad
\operatorname{Ric}\geq0,
\]
such that
\[
\operatorname{rank}\operatorname{Ric}=
\begin{cases}
3,&t=0,\\
4,&0<|t|<\varepsilon.
\end{cases}
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The case $n=4$ follows from
Proposition~\ref{prop:shrinker-4d-counterexample}. For $n>4$, take the
product of this soliton with the Gaussian shrinking soliton
\[
\left(
\mathbb R^{n-4},
g_{\mathrm{Euc}},
\frac{|z|^2}{4}
\right).
\]
Thus
\[
\widehat M
=
M_\varepsilon\times\mathbb R^{n-4},
\qquad
\widehat g
=
g+g_{\mathrm{Euc}},
\qquad
\widehat\phi
=
\phi+\frac{|z|^2}{4}.
\]
Then
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_{\widehat g}+\nabla^2\widehat\phi
=
 \frac{1}{2} \widehat g,
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_{\widehat g}
=
\operatorname{Ric}_g\oplus0
\geq0.
\]
Its rank equals $3$ along $t=0$ and $4$ for
$0<|t|<\varepsilon$, so it is not constant.

Finally, the same examples show directly that the endpoint
$\operatorname{Ric}_{n-1}=\operatorname{Ric}\geq0$ cannot replace the assumption
$\operatorname{Ric}_k\geq0$, $k\leq n-2$. At $t=0$, fix the direction $e_3$.
The sectional curvatures involving $e_3$ are
\[
-3,\quad\frac{3}{2},\quad\frac{3}{2},\quad
\underbrace{0,\ldots,0}_{n-4}.
\]
Among the $n-1$ orthogonal directions, choose the $n-2$ directions
obtained by omitting one of the two directions with curvature $\frac{3}{2}$.
Their sum is $-\frac{3}{2}$. Hence
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_{n-2}\not\geq0.
\]
This proves both the theorem and the sharpness of the range
$1\leq k\leq n-2$.

title: Remark
body_md:
The counterexample above is local, since the constant-rank conclusion
in Theorem~\ref{thm:mainB} is itself local and does not require
completeness. It is a separate question whether there exists a complete
gradient Ricci soliton with $\operatorname{Ric}\geq0$ and nonconstant Ricci rank. For recent related work, see \cite{Wu-Wu2}.
